question: What is write-ahead logging (WAL) in database systems?

evidence.text: EVORAG | DBMS & SQL KNOWLEDGE BASE POSTGRESQL 18 REFERENCE BASELINE Educational retrieval corpus-original explanations with cited references Page 2 2. Logging and write-ahead logging A log records enough information to recover the database. A simplified update log record may contain a transaction identifier, page or record identifier, and before/after information. Undo logging uses old values; redo logging uses new values; undo/redo logging retains both or otherwise carries sufficient recovery data. Actual engines use more complex log formats, page identifiers, sequence numbers, checksums, and transaction state. The write-ahead logging principle requires the log record describing a change to be flushed to durable storage before the changed data page is allowed to be written. If a crash occurs after a data page was written but before its log record became durable, recovery might not know how to repair it.

results.answer: Write-ahead logging (WAL) is a technique used in database systems to ensure data integrity and prevent data loss in the event of a system failure or restart.WAL works by writing a log of all changes made to the database to a separate storage area, called the log file.This log is written in advance of the changes being made to the database, hence the name "write-ahead logging."If a system failure or restart occurs, the database can use the log file to recover the changes that were made since the last checkpoint, without having to read the data from the database itself.This means that the database can continue to operate without interruption, even if there is a failure or restart
